additional_concerns: The candidate's conjunctive test of retained accountability, effective supervision and satisfactory outcomes is an interpretation, not an express three-part test in paragraph 10. The excerpts establish neither a reasonable-care safe harbour nor strict liability for every adverse outcome.
Section 6.11C concerns third-party valuation. Its reasonable-care and supervision standard cannot be transferred to tokenisation responsibility without an applicability basis.

Section 6.8 permits register maintenance by specified parties while footnote 1 preserves provider responsibility. Delegated maintenance neither transfers ultimate responsibility nor proves substantive fulfilment.

The supplied intermediary paragraph 13 concerns issuers or intermediaries substantially involved in issuance. Role overlap requires facts; this provision cannot automatically substitute for the Product Provider's obligation.

Paragraph 15 separately requires third-party audit or verification upon request; paragraph 16 concerns a legal opinion supporting an application. Neither supplies an automatic substantive-compliance safe harbour.

The applicable adequacy standard, assessment period, incident materiality and remediation treatment remain unresolved. Obtain applicable Part A Appendix factors and relevant regulatory guidance, together with actual accountability, supervision, compatibility and ownership-record evidence. Missing evidence must not become a false compliance result.
No executable meaning is supplied. Retrieval results and the unsupported structural-tool result establish no legal correctness.
